proposals.lesson: When the owner designates an existing real-workload baseline, lock the exact artifact hashes and run only new candidates. Preserve runtime differences as an explicit caveat; do not silently relabel the old configuration.
proposals.evidence: quick32-v3 completed 32/32 natural-stop requests with zero errors at concurrency 1, 5, 8 and 16

proposals.lesson: One variable is an attribution step, not a final-stack constraint. Measure a treatment alone, retain it only after correctness and performance gates, add it to the current best stack, and keep ablations while comparing every stack with the same original.
proposals.evidence: FlashComm1, BF16 FRACTAL_NZ and their non-quantized cumulative launcher/config are isolated

proposals.lesson: Natural EOS includes empty-text EOS-only completions; benchmark TTFT from the first token event. Reject an optimization even when transport succeeds if response hashes diverge.
proposals.evidence: The harness correction recovered four valid EOS-only requests; Qwen3.5 MTP was rejected with 16-21 response mismatches and latency regressions

proposals.lesson: A documented dense communication optimization is not stack-eligible until the target architecture survives graph construction. On Qwen3.5 TP4, FlashComm1 activated sequence parallelism and normalized graph sizes, but the GDN graph retained an unsplit symbolic sequence length and failed before readiness. Classify this as an implementation/runtime failure, not a performance regression or rejection of the general method.
proposals.evidence: Run flashcomm1-fixedorig-npu4-7-20260904T1816Z; service.log SHA256 35ef543dd9ab29d127ce01b2556b6abf8b0a46e9068320f7a97d4e69cf59e692; operation exec-000000000000053a exited 70 before any benchmark cell

proposals.lesson: Static support for BF16 FRACTAL_NZ and MatMulAllReduce does not imply composability. On this v0.23.0 path, NZ weight transformation succeeded, but aclnnMatmulAllReduce required x2 in ND and failed before readiness. Record this as an interaction failure and test NZ with the fixed original's MatMulAllReduce-disabled setting before rejecting the layout itself.
proposals.evidence: Run bf16-nz-fixedorig-npu4-7-20260904T1838Z; service.log SHA256 0756f2a7770166afa54d4e4ff08178be13d6b81287a28fa861ec9e1b3ddf82b9; operation exec-000000000000056e exited 70

proposals.lesson: A treatment can deliver a real median win in part of the matrix and still be rejected. BF16 FRACTAL_NZ with MatMulAllReduce disabled roughly halved c1/c5 TTFT, but it changed exact outputs, missed the TPOT target, and regressed c16 TTFT. Preserve the useful locality signal without promoting the treatment to the cumulative stack.

When a nominally semantics-preserving communication switch changes exact response hashes and produces a large TTFT shift across a different physical device set, do not credit the whole delta to the switch. Keep the owner-designated original immutable, but run a no-op control candidate on the assigned devices to quantify run/device drift before accepting correctness criteria or performance attribution.
proposals.evidence: MMAR-only run mmar-on-fixedorig-npu4-7-20260904T1921Z completed all cells but mismatched 17/20/17/15 response hashes; decision SHA256 870c8f04911b838670d4e0414b3846d14fa7cb2cb0774b15230a573f681ecc0b

proposals.lesson: If a no-op control with the same model, seed and runtime switches changes many output hashes, exact equality to a historical run is not a calibrated semantic correctness gate. Keep the hashes as a diagnostic, fail closed, and add privacy-safe aggregate comparison to labeled references before accepting a treatment.
proposals.evidence: Control run control-mmar-off-fixedorig-npu4-7-20260904T1943Z differed from the original in 15/15/19/16 hashes; control decision SHA256 ff77a6fc8aadbf6d0561834b9f42a12a562cee76f5da4c4a6f9ae68eaf803b39

proposals.lesson: Continue reporting every candidate against the owner-designated fixed denominator, but also use a same-device no-op control for causal attribution. In this run the fixed-original comparison suggested large MMAR gains, while the same-device control reduced net TPOT gain to 0-5.3% and c1-c8 TTFT gain to 2.4-8.6%.
proposals.evidence: MMAR run mmar-on-fixedorig-npu4-7-20260904T1921Z versus control run control-mmar-off-fixedorig-npu4-7-20260904T1943Z

proposals.lesson: On vLLM 0.23.0 multiprocess TP, disabling async scheduling is not sufficient to make torch_npu profiling safe. The worker profiler is lazily constructed through a profile RPC thread, while CANN requires external profiler initialization on the registerClient thread. Preserve the failure and switch the collection mechanism rather than weakening inference semantics.
proposals.evidence: Run fixed-runtime-mmar-off-npu4-7-20260904T2004Z; operation exec-0000000000000659; /stop_profile returned 500 after TP0 exited and the executor was canceled

proposals.lesson: For a long-lived Ascend inference service whose framework profiler lifecycle is broken, set PROFILING_MODE=dynamic before startup and use msprof attach to bracket a real request. In TP workloads collect one worker/device at a time, keep the profile diagnostic-only, and export op_summary for hotspot ranking.
proposals.evidence: NPU4 smoke operation exec-000000000000066f completed start/stop/quit and export; one op_summary contained 41119 operator calls

proposals.lesson: Rank hotspot totals by request phase before choosing an optimization. Dynamic attach captured one 173830us AllReduce before the detected prefill window, while steady AllReduce p50/p95 were only 22.86/23.70us. The outlier is evidence of startup or synchronization cost, not a representative collective kernel latency.

When dense decode is dominated by low-batch GEMMs, test training-free verified multi-token execution before rewriting a low-share state-space operator. On vLLM-Ascend use the NPU ngram proposer when async scheduling is frozen; the CPU ngram proposer is incompatible with async scheduling.
proposals.evidence: Post-prefill rank-0 window: MatMulV2 70.702%, AllReduce 10.530%, recurrent GDN 2.406%; exact image dispatches ngram_gpu to npu_ngram_spec_decode
